mainTopic: Pouring waste water on שבת: courtyard size, the seasons, pit capacity, and facing apartments
overview: The משנה allows pouring water on שבת into a courtyard of four by four אמות, even though it may run out into רשות הרבים. A smaller courtyard needs an עוקה, a pit to catch the water. רבה says a big courtyard is worth sprinkling, while רבי זירא says a big courtyard absorbs the water. אביי shows that they differ over a long, narrow courtyard. The גמרא tests both views against the משנה and a ברייתא, and concludes that the whole משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, for whom four אמות of space is what counts. Next the גמרא notes that חנניא forbids pouring even onto a huge roof, and a ברייתא says the limits apply only in summer. רבא and אביי explain why the rainy season is lenient, and רב נחמן sets rules for pit sizes in each season. Finally, רבא rules about two facing upper apartments even if they made an עירוב. אביי refutes that version with a ברייתא, so the גמרא begins a corrected version of רבא's words, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבה's rule for a courtyard smaller than four cubits
steps.stepSummary: Completing רבה's explanation: in a courtyard under four אמות a person just pours the water away. So it is allowed only with an עוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the courtyard is less than four אמות, he simply pours the water out. So if he made a pit, it is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבה's explanation of the משנה. A small courtyard is not worth sprinkling, so the person is just getting rid of the water, and he needs a pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of רבה's statement, on the previous amud, said that in a four-אמות courtyard a person wants to sprinkle the floor to settle the dust. So the water spilling outside is not his intention. In a smaller courtyard there is no sprinkling benefit, so he is plainly dumping the water and it will run into רשות הרבים. That is why an עוקה is required there.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than four (אמות by four אמות)
He pours them out, simply dumping the water
A pit dug to collect the poured water

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion starting here. It is the second half of רבה's statement, which began on the previous amud with the four-אמות case (sprinkling).

phrases.english: Less than four — he pours them out.
phrases.notes: There is no sprinkling benefit, so he just dumps the water.

phrases.english: If he made a pit — it is permitted,
if not — it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Without a pit, the water will clearly run out to the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's explanation on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבה, the four-אמות threshold depends on whether the courtyard is worth sprinkling. A smaller courtyard needs an עוקה.

steps.title: רבי זירא's reason: absorption
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains the four-אמות rule differently. A four-אמות area absorbs the water, while a smaller area does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: four אמות absorb the water. Less than four אמות do not absorb it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא offers a second explanation of the same משנה. The issue is not sprinkling but whether the ground soaks up the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי זירא, a courtyard with an area of four by four אמות is big enough for the water to sink into the ground before it reaches the street. A smaller area cannot absorb it, so the water flows out. The four-אמות size is therefore about total area, not about the courtyard's usefulness.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives an alternative reason
They absorb (the water soaks into the ground)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Four cubits — they absorb,
less than four cubits — they do not absorb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing reason for the same four-אמות rule that רבה explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four-אמות threshold depends on whether the area can absorb the water.

steps.title: What is the practical difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the two explanations differ in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: Both opinions agree on the basic rule, so the גמרא asks what case would come out differently. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה and רבי זירא give different reasons but seem to reach the same result in an ordinary square courtyard. The גמרא wants a case where the different reasons lead to different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the (practical) difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical difference between the two reasons just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רבה and רבי זירא would rule differently.

steps.title: אביי: a long and narrow courtyard
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the difference is a courtyard that is long and narrow, with the full area but not a square shape.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the difference between them is a long and narrow courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the case where the two opinions split: a courtyard with sixteen square אמות of area that is not square, for example eight by two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי זירא, only area matters. A long, narrow courtyard has enough area to absorb the water, so no pit is needed. According to רבה, a narrow strip is not the kind of courtyard people sprinkle, so he is just dumping the water and needs an עוקה.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who identifies the practical difference

steps.whatToRemember: רבה looks at the shape and usefulness of the courtyard (is it worth sprinkling?). רבי זירא looks only at total area (can it absorb the water?). A long, narrow courtyard is permitted without a pit according to רבי זירא, but needs a pit according to רבה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Long and narrow is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: For example, 8×2 אמות: the same area as 4×4, but not square.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֲרִיךְ וְקַטִּין אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the practical difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A long, narrow courtyard. רבי זירא permits it without a pit (enough area to absorb). רבה requires a pit (not fit for sprinkling).

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: courtyard and portico combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the משנה's rule that a courtyard and a portico combine to reach four אמות. This sets up a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: a courtyard and a portico combine to make four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from our משנה to set up its next move, a test of the two opinions. This step is not the challenge yet; it supplies the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if the courtyard alone is too small, the attached portico (a roofed porch area) can be added to reach four אמות. Combining two areas usually produces an irregular, non-square shape. That point will matter in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A portico, a roofed porch open on one side
They combine (to make up the required size)

phrases.english: We learned: a courtyard and a portico
combine for four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: חָצֵר וְאַכְסַדְרָה מִצְטָרְפִין לְאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to test the two opinions against.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's sprinkling explanation (stated fully in the next step).

steps.title: The משנה fits רבי זירא but is difficult for רבה
steps.stepSummary: Combining courtyard and portico works for רבי זירא, since the area adds up. It is difficult for רבה, since the combined shape is not a square fit for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רבי זירא it works out well. But according to רבה it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה from the משנה. Combining a courtyard with a portico makes sense if only area matters, but not if the courtyard must be a sprinkle-worthy square.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי זירא, the combined spaces give enough area to absorb the water, so the משנה is easy. For רבה, the combined space is no longer a square courtyard, much like the long, narrow case in which he required a pit. So why does the משנה allow combining? The next step answers this challenge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge uses אביי's distinction directly. Because רבה cares about the shape of the courtyard, any combined, irregular space is a problem for him.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Zeira it works out well,
phrases.notes: The total area adds up, so the water is absorbed.

phrases.english: but according to Rabba it is difficult!
phrases.notes: The combined area is not a square fit for sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי זֵירָא נִיחָא, אֶלָּא לְרַבָּה קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the quoted משנה as a challenge against רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that the four-אמות rule depends on the courtyard being fit for sprinkling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A courtyard combined with a portico is not a square shape fit for sprinkling, yet the משנה lets them combine. This matches רבי זירא's area-based reasoning but contradicts רבה's sprinkling-based reasoning.

steps.title: רבי זירא defends רבה: the portico runs along the whole courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers the challenge against רבה. The משנה about a courtyard and portico combining speaks of a portico that runs along the entire length of the courtyard. Together they form a proper square.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא explained the משנה according to רבה: it speaks of a portico that runs along the whole length of the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 6 against רבה. Surprisingly, the one defending רבה is רבי זירא, his opponent in this debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that a courtyard plus a portico would make an odd shape, not a square fit for sprinkling. רבי זירא answers that the portico runs the full length of the courtyard and only adds width. So the two together make a real four-by-four square, which fits רבה's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Portico; a roofed area open on the sides, attached to the courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up: רבי זירא disagrees with רבה, but here he answers on רבה's behalf. The גמרא sometimes shows one side helping the other side's position.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira explained it according to Rabbah:
It refers to a portico that runs
along the entire length of the courtyard.
phrases.notes: So the portico only adds width, and the combined area forms a proper square.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 6 against רבה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the portico runs along the full length of the courtyard
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Courtyard plus portico makes an irregular shape, so the משנה contradicts רבה
steps.terutzMaskana: The combined area forms a true square, so the משנה fits רבה's reason

steps.title: A ברייתא that fits רבה but challenges רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a courtyard that is not four אמות by four אמות may not have water poured into it. That sounds like it needs a square shape, which supports רבה and challenges רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a courtyard that does not have four אמות by four אמות, one may not pour water into it on שבת. This works for רבה, but it is difficult for רבי זירא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to test the debate. It fits רבה and is a problem for רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'four by four', which sounds like a square shape is required. For רבה that is exactly the point. For רבי זירא only the total area matters, so a long, narrow courtyard with enough area should be permitted. But the ברייתא's wording seems to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a source to prove or challenge
It is understandable (according to one view)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A courtyard that does not have
four cubits by four cubits —
one may not pour water into it on Shabbat.
Granted, according to Rabbah it works out well,
but according to Rabbi Zeira it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבה, the גמרא now brings a new source that challenges רבי זירא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's view that the total area (absorption) is what matters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires four by four, implying a square shape. A long, narrow courtyard with enough area would be forbidden, which contradicts רבי זירא.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the ברייתא follows the רבנן, our משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the ברייתא follows the רבנן, who do not care about area. Our משנה, which he explains, follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, for whom area is what matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא can say to you: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is the רבנן. Our משנה is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא escapes the challenge. He says the ברייתא and our משנה follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Later in the משנה, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב focuses on how much space there is to absorb the water. The רבנן disagree and say area does not help. So רבי זירא can say his absorption reason explains רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view in our משנה. The ברייתא, requiring a square, reflects the רבנן's different approach.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you; introduces how a sage would answer
A תנא in the משנה who focuses on the area that absorbs the water

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira can say to you:
Whose view is this? It is the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא.
phrases.english: while our Mishnah is Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה share one view, so the ברייתא disproves רבי זירא
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the רבנן; רבי זירא's reason explains רבי אליעזר בן יעקב in our משנה
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא tool: when a source contradicts an אמורא, he may say it reflects a different תנא, so he does not need to agree with it.

steps.title: Why did רבי זירא need to assign the משנה to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what forced רבי זירא to say our unattributed משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, rather than the majority view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what pushed רבי זירא to explain our משנה according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי זירא chose this harder reading. This question sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we prefer to read an unattributed משנה like the רבנן, the majority view. Assigning it to one individual תנא is a 'stretch'. The גמרא wants to know what in the משנה made רבי זירא take that path.

keyTerms.meaning: What forced him? What pressure pushed him?

phrases.english: And what forced Rabbi Zeira
to establish our Mishnah
according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason behind the answer in Step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the משנה pushed רבי זירא to attribute it to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב instead of the רבנן

steps.title: רבא: the משנה's word 'less than' pointed to area
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה's wording bothered רבי זירא. It says 'a courtyard that is less', which points to total area. If a square shape mattered, it should have said 'that does not have four by four'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה was difficult for him. Why did it say 'a courtyard that is less'? It should have said 'a courtyard that does not have four אמות by four אמות'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from Step 10. He shows the exact word in the משנה that pushed רבי זירא to his reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Less than four by four' measures total size, about sixteen square אמות. That suggests a long, narrow courtyard with enough area is fine, which is רבי זירא's view. Had the משנה cared about shape, it would have used the ברייתא's wording, 'does not have four by four'. So רבי זירא saw that the משנה is about area and matched it to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? Why this wording?
Let it teach; it should have said

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's wording ('does not have four by four') points to shape and fits רבה. The משנה's wording ('less than') points to area and fits רבי זירא. So רבי זירא reads the משנה as רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the ברייתא as the רבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: The two wordings sound almost the same in English. The point: 'less than' measures total size, while 'does not have four by four' means it lacks a full square.

phrases.english: Rava said: The Mishnah was difficult for him,
why did it specifically teach
'a courtyard that is less',
let it teach: 'a courtyard that does not have
four cubits by four cubits'!
phrases.notes: That wording would have pointed to shape. Saying 'less' points to total area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה's word 'פחותה' points to total area, not a square shape. This matches רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's focus on area, so רבי זירא attributed the משנה to him.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי זירא's absorption view rests on the משנה's wording, read as רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. The ברייתא's square-shape wording follows the רבנן.

steps.title: So the opening of the משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: Based on רבא's reading of the wording 'less than', the גמרא concludes that the unattributed opening of the משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not learn from this that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבא's explanation. Because the משנה says 'less than', which is about total area, it must follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11, רבא showed that the wording 'less than four אמות' points to total area, not to a square shape. Area is what matters to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, so this explains why רבי זירא gave the משנה to him. The closing 'שמע מינה' confirms the point.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that... (introduces the forced conclusion)
Learn from it. Used both to propose a conclusion and to confirm it.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this,
that it follows Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?
Yes, learn from it.
phrases.notes: The גמרא confirms the conclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer from Step 11 and states the conclusion it leads to.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The opening line of the משנה (a courtyard 'less than four אמות') follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, for whom area is what matters.

steps.title: But the end of the משנה names him, so the beginning must be someone else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the conclusion. The משנה names רבי אליעזר בן יעקב only in a later clause, which implies the first clause is not his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the end of the משנה is said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, that implies the beginning is not רבי אליעזר בן יעקב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the conclusion from Step 12 by pointing to how the משנה is built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, when a משנה names a תנא only in its last part, the earlier unnamed part belongs to someone else, such as the majority. Here the סיפא says 'רבי אליעזר בן יעקב אומר'. That suggests the רישא, the courtyard rule, is not his. If so, it cannot be the source for his view about area.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part (later clause) of a משנה
The first part (opening clause) of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not about the law of courtyards. It is about structure: who is speaking in each part of the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: But since the latter clause is Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא לָאו רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב!
phrases.english: the first clause is not Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion just reached in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the unattributed רישא of the משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תנא named only in the סיפא implies that the earlier unnamed רישא belongs to a different view.

steps.title: The whole משנה is his, and some words are missing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the entire משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Some words are missing, and the restored text links the courtyard rule to his ruling about an arched drain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole משנה is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, but it is missing words, and this is what it teaches: A courtyard less than four אמות may not have water poured into it on שבת. This implies that if it is four אמות, one may pour, because רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: a drain arched over for four אמות in the public domain may have water poured into it on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its conclusion. It says the משנה has a gap and fills in the missing words so the whole משנה reads as רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His name appears in the סיפא only because the סיפא gives the reason for the רישא, not because it disagrees with it. The restored line says: since less than four אמות is forbidden, four אמות is allowed. That matches his ruling that four אמות of arched drain is enough. In both cases the deciding factor is four אמות of space.

keyTerms.meaning: It is missing words. The text is incomplete and must be filled in.
And this is what it teaches (introduces the restored text)
This implies... (draws the opposite case from a rule)

steps.whatToRemember: Through חסורי מחסרא, the whole משנה becomes one view. The courtyard rule (four אמות is enough) and the arched-drain rule both come from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.confusionAlert: חסורי מחסרא does not mean the משנה is wrong. It means some words are understood but not written, and the גמרא spells them out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבי זירא's approach. His explanation of the משנה as being about area depends on the משנה following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא,
phrases.english: The entire משנה is Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,
and it is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
A courtyard that is less than four cubits,
one may not pour water into it on Shabbat;
this implies that if it is four cubits, one may pour,
phrases.notes: This is the restored, missing line.

phrases.english: because Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:

phrases.aramaic: בִּיב הַקָּמוּר אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים —
phrases.english: a drain arched over for four cubits in the public domain,
one may pour water into it on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא, וְחַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the structural challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual reconstruction (חסורי מחסרא): the משנה is read as incomplete and the missing words are restored.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming רבי אליעזר בן יעקב in the סיפא meant the רישא belonged to a different view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא gives the reason for the רישא. The whole משנה is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and four אמות of space is the deciding measure in both rulings.

steps.title: Quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב on the arched drain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: an arched drain' to open a new discussion of that ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: An arched drain.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the opening words of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling from the משנה to begin discussing it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard discussion is finished. Now the גמרא turns to the arched-drain ruling itself. This short quote acts as a heading, and the actual analysis will follow in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Arched over, covered with a vault

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
An arched drain.
phrases.notes: Quotes the משנה as a heading for the next discussion.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: בִּיב הַקָּמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the courtyard discussion ends in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quoted from the משנה: according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, one may pour water on שבת into a drain arched over for four אמות in the public domain.

steps.title: Our משנה does not follow חנניא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the משנה disagrees with חנניא. It then quotes a ברייתא where חנניא says that even a 100-אמה roof cannot be used to pour water on שבת, because a roof does not absorb water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow חנניא. For a ברייתא teaches: חנניא says, even onto a roof of 100 אמות one may not pour water, because a roof is not made to absorb water, only to let it run off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the משנה holds one view and חנניא holds another. It quotes חנניא's ruling to show where they disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (the רבנן) permits pouring water onto a roof, from which it runs down into the drain. חנניא says size does not help with a roof, because a hard roof surface never soaks water in. The water just runs off into the public domain, so pouring onto it is like pouring straight outside.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who is strict about pouring water onto a roof
To make water flow or run off
For it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: חנניא's point is not about how big the roof is. Even a huge roof fails, because the surface itself does not absorb water.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is not in accordance with Chananya.
For it was taught in a baraita: Chananya says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ גַּג מֵאָה אַמָּה — לֹא יִשְׁפּוֹךְ,
phrases.english: Even a roof of one hundred cubits, one may not pour onto it,
because a roof is not made to absorb water,
phrases.notes: A roof is hard, so water does not soak in.

phrases.english: but rather to make it run off.
phrases.notes: The water ends up flowing into the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Places the משנה's rules about pouring water alongside a competing תנאי view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה disagrees with חנניא, who forbids pouring onto even a 100-אמה roof because a roof does not absorb water.

steps.title: The restrictions apply only in summer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא limits the pouring restrictions to the summer. In the rainy season one may pour as much as he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: When do these rules apply? In the summer. But in the rainy season, one may pour, pour again, and need not hold back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that narrows all these pouring rules to the summer months only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the rules about needing enough space or a ditch sounded like they applied all year. This ברייתא adds a new limit: in the rainy season there is no restriction at all. The reason is not given yet. The גמרא asks for it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case were these words said? (a formula that limits a rule)

phrases.english: A tanna taught: In what case are these words said?
In the summer;
but in the rainy season,
one may pour and pour again, and need not hold back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a seasonal limit to the pouring restrictions discussed so far.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pouring restrictions apply only in summer. In the rainy season one may pour freely.

steps.title: Why is the rainy season different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rainy-season leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why one may pour freely in the rainy season. This question sets up רבא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water poured in winter could still flow out into the public domain, just as in summer. So the leniency needs a reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why pouring is allowed freely in the rainy season.

steps.title: רבא: in winter he is fine with the water soaking in where it is
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that in the rainy season a person is happy for the water to be absorbed right where it lands. So we do not suspect him of trying to send it outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A person is willing for the water to be absorbed in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question of why winter is lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In winter the courtyard is already wet and muddy, so the owner does not mind if the extra water stays there. Since he is not trying to push the water out to the public domain, there is no reason to forbid pouring.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the rainy-season leniency
In their place, right where they land

phrases.english: Rava said:
A person is willing for the water to be absorbed in its place.
phrases.notes: The courtyard is already wet from the rain, so he does not mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָדָם רוֹצֶה שֶׁיִּבָּלְעוּ מַיִם בִּמְקוֹמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the rainy season a person does not mind the water staying in his courtyard, so he has no intent to send it out.

steps.title: אביי: waste water is also wanted to soak in, yet it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא's reason. With waste water, a person also wants it absorbed, yet the משנה says not to pour it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But look at waste water, which a person wants to be absorbed, and yet the משנה teaches 'one may not pour'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's explanation by pointing to a case where the same reasoning fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'he wants it to soak in' were enough to permit pouring, then waste water should be permitted too. But the משנה forbids it. So אביי argues that this reason cannot explain the winter leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who argues with רבא

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But there is waste water, which a person wants to be absorbed,
and yet the Mishnah teaches 'one may not pour'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reason from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason that wanting the water absorbed permits pouring
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Waste water is also wanted absorbed, yet the משנה forbids pouring it. So that reason cannot be what permits pouring.

steps.title: רבא: in winter neither concern applies
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that in the rainy season there is nothing to worry about. The courtyard is already muddy, and gutters flowing with water are normal, so no one becomes suspicious.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, what should we worry about? If it is because he wants to avoid ruining his courtyard, it is already ruined. And if it is because of a גזירה, that people may say 'so-and-so's gutter is pouring water', in winter gutters usually flow anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the winter leniency by showing that both reasons for forbidding pouring fall away in the rainy season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible reasons to forbid pouring. First, the owner may want the water to flow outside so his courtyard stays clean. In winter it is already muddy, so he has no such motive. Second, the רבנן made a גזירה so people will not see his gutter flowing and draw the wrong conclusion. In winter every gutter flows from the rain, so no one notices. Waste water in summer is different, because these concerns do apply then.
steps.whatToRemember: In the rainy season one may pour water freely on שבת. The courtyard is already muddy, so he has no motive to send the water out, and flowing gutters are normal, so there is no fear of what people will say.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a rabbinic restriction disappears when the reasons behind it do not apply in that situation.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There, what should we be concerned about?
phrases.notes: "There" means the rainy season.

phrases.english: If it is because of ruining his courtyard,
it is already ruined.
phrases.notes: The rain has already made it muddy.

phrases.english: And if it is because of a decree, lest people say,
'So-and-so's gutter is pouring out water',
gutters ordinarily flow anyway.
phrases.notes: In winter, rain makes every gutter flow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם לְמַאי נֵיחוּשׁ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: both reasons for the restriction are missing in the rainy season.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wanting the water to be absorbed alone permits pouring, so waste water should be permitted too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Winter is lenient because the courtyard is already ruined and flowing gutters are normal. Both concerns behind the restriction disappear.

steps.title: רב נחמן sets pit-size rules for rainy season and summer
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that in ימות הגשמים one may pour into an עוקה as much as it holds, whether two סאה or one סאה. In ימות החמה a two-סאה pit may be used, but a one-סאה pit may not be used at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: In the rainy season, if a pit holds two סאה, we let him pour two סאה into it. If it holds one סאה, we let him pour one סאה. In the summer, if it holds two סאה, we let him pour two סאה. But if it holds only one סאה, we do not let him pour into it at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a new, more exact rule about how big the pit must be, and the rule is different in each season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the rainy season, a pit of any size can be used, as long as he pours only what it holds. In the summer, a two-סאה pit is allowed, but a smaller pit is completely forbidden. The next steps will explain why the summer is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: A small pit or hollow in the courtyard that collects water
Two סאה. This is the amount of water a person normally uses in a day

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'holds one סאה, we give it one סאה' (rainy season, allowed) with 'one סאה, we give it nothing at all' (summer, forbidden). Same pit size, opposite rulings, depending on the season.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
In the rainy season,
a pit that holds two se'a:
we allow him two se'a,
if it holds one se'a, we allow him one se'a.
In the summer,
if it holds two se'a, we allow him two se'a,

phrases.aramaic: סְאָה — אֵין נוֹתְנִין לוֹ כָּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: if it holds one se'a, we do not allow him anything at all.
phrases.notes: The pit may not be used at all, not even for one סאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds exact pit-size rules to the rainy-season versus summer distinction set up in Steps 17-21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rainy season: a pit of any size may be used, up to what it holds. Summer: only a pit that holds two סאה may be used. A one-סאה pit is completely forbidden.

steps.title: Why not allow one סאה in a one-סאה pit in summer too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the summer rule. If he pours only one סאה into a one-סאה pit, nothing will overflow, so why not allow it?
steps.simpleTranslation: In the summer too, if the pit holds one סאה, let us allow him to pour one סאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב נחמן's summer rule. Pouring only what the pit holds should be safe in any season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the restriction is fear that water will flow out into the street. If the amount poured matches the pit's size, nothing flows out. So the total ban on a small pit in summer seems to have no reason.

phrases.english: In the summer too,
if it holds one se'a, let us allow him one se'a!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה נָמֵי, מַחֲזִיק סְאָה נִיתֵּיב לֵיהּ סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the summer half of רב נחמן's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's total ban on a one-סאה pit in the summer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rainy-season rule (pour up to capacity) should also work in summer, because pouring only up to capacity causes no overflow.

steps.title: A גזירה in case he pours two סאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the summer ban is a גזירה. If we allowed him to use a small pit, he might pour his usual two סאה, and the extra would flow out into the street.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, in case he comes to pour two סאה into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the summer ban is a protective decree (גזירה), not a problem with the one סאה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person normally uses about two סאה of water. With a one-סאה pit he might pour it all, and the extra would run out into רשות הרבים. In summer he actually wants that, so his courtyard stays dry. So the rabbis forbade the small pit entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic protective decree that forbids something permitted, to stop a person from coming to a real problem

phrases.aramaic: גְּזֵרָה דִּלְמָא אָתֵי לִיתֵּן לֵיהּ סָאתַיִם.
phrases.english: It is a decree, lest he come to put two se'a into it.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵרָה דִּלְמָא אָתֵי לִיתֵּן לֵיהּ סָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב נחמן's summer rule against the challenge in Step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pouring one סאה into a one-סאה pit is harmless, so it should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is forbidden as a safeguard, because he may pour his usual two סאה and cause overflow into the street.

steps.title: Then make the same decree in the rainy season
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. If we fear he will pour two סאה into a small pit, the same fear should apply in the rainy season.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us also make this decree in the rainy season!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around. The same גזירה should forbid small pits in the rainy season too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fear that he will pour too much has nothing to do with the season. So רב נחמן's leniency for a one-סאה pit in the rainy season now looks inconsistent.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים נָמֵי לִיגְזוֹר!
phrases.english: If so, in the rainy season let us also decree!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים נָמֵי לִיגְזוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of Step 24 to attack the rainy-season half of רב נחמן's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rainy-season permission for a one-סאה pit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason for the summer ban is fear of over-pouring, that fear exists in every season, so the decree should apply in winter too.

steps.title: In the rainy season there is nothing to worry about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even if he pours too much in the rainy season, nothing bad happens. The courtyard is already muddy, and every gutter is flowing anyway, so no one will suspect him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, in the rainy season, what should we worry about? If it is because he wants to keep his courtyard from being ruined, it is already ruined by the rain. If it is because of the decree 'people may say so-and-so's gutter is pouring water,' gutters normally pour water then.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why no decree is needed in the rainy season. Both possible worries simply do not exist then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A decree only makes sense if over-pouring leads to a real problem. In summer he wants the water to flow out to keep his courtyard dry, and people would notice his gutter flowing. In the rainy season the courtyard is already muddy and all gutters flow, so over-pouring causes no problem and no decree is needed.
steps.confusionAlert: This repeats the reasoning from Steps 19-21 on purpose. Before, it explained why the rainy season is lenient. Here, it is used to answer why no גזירה is needed in the rainy season.

phrases.english: There, what should we be concerned about?
If because of ruining the courtyard,
it is already ruined.
phrases.notes: The rain has already made the courtyard muddy.

phrases.english: If because of the decree

phrases.aramaic: ״שֶׁמָּא יֹאמְרוּ צִנּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי מְקַלֵּחַ מַיִם״ —
phrases.english: 'lest people say: so-and-so's gutter is gushing water,'
gutters ordinarily gush then.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25 by repeating the reasoning of Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the reason for the decree does not apply in the rainy season
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fear of over-pouring should lead to a decree in every season.
steps.terutzMaskana: Over-pouring in the rainy season causes no real problem (no reason to ruin anything, no suspicion), so no decree is needed.

steps.title: אביי: in the rainy season, even huge amounts are allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes that since there is no concern in the rainy season, one may pour even a כור or two כור of water, even into a small pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Therefore, even a כור and even two כור.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws the final practical result from the reasoning in Step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If over-pouring causes no problem in the rainy season, the pit's size does not matter at all. So the amount has no limit, even a כור (thirty סאה) or two. This also matches the ברייתא in Step 17: in the rainy season one pours as much as he wants.

keyTerms.meaning: A large measure, equal to thirty סאה

steps.whatToRemember: Summer: only a pit that holds two סאה may be used, because of a גזירה that he may over-pour and send water into the street. Rainy season: there is no concern at all, so one may pour any amount, even a כור or two, as אביי concludes.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key principle about rabbinic decrees: a גזירה applies only where its underlying worry actually exists.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Therefore, even a kor and even two kor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical conclusion from the reasoning in Step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the rainy season there is no limit on the amount of waste water one may pour, even into a small pit.

steps.title: Two facing upper apartments and רבא's ruling about an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about two upper apartments facing each other. רבא adds that the rule holds even if they made an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, two upper apartments facing each other in the same courtyard: the residents of the one that dug a pit may pour water, and the residents of the other may not. רבא said: this is true even if they made an עירוב together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its next case: two upper apartments facing each other across one courtyard. רבא then comments that the משנה's rule still applies even if the two apartments joined in an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, only the apartment that made a proper pit (עוקה) may pour water into the courtyard on שבת. You would expect an עירוב, which joins the two households, to let both use the pit. רבא says the עירוב does not change the rule, so the second apartment still may not pour.

keyTerms.meaning: Upper-story apartments (lofts) that open onto a shared courtyard
One opposite the other, facing each other across the courtyard
They made an עירוב, joining their properties so carrying between them is allowed
Even, introducing a more surprising case to which the rule still applies

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is saying the עירוב makes things more lenient. His point is that even with an עירוב, the apartment without the pit is still not allowed to pour.

phrases.english: And likewise, two upper apartments
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: one opposite the other.
phrases.notes: In the משנה, one made a pit and one did not

phrases.english: Rava said: even if they made an eruv.
phrases.notes: The rule stands even with an עירוב

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי דְיוֹטָאוֹת זוֹ כְּנֶגֶד זוֹ. אָמַר רָבָא: אֲפִילּוּ עֵירְבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from אביי's conclusion about the rainy season to the next case in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even if the two upper apartments made an עירוב, the משנה's rule still applies: the residents of the apartment without the pit may not pour.

steps.title: אביי asks for the reason and suggests one
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks why the עירוב makes no difference, and suggests the reason might be the larger amount of water.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What is the reason for this? If you say it is because there is more water, since two households pour more than one...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks רבא why an עירוב would not help. He proposes a possible reason: two households together pour out too much water for one pit. This is a setup, because the next step will knock down this reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested logic is that once the two apartments join through the עירוב, both will pour into the same pit. That doubles the water, so the pit might overflow into the public street. The word אילימא tells us this explanation is being put forward only so it can be tested.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, introducing a suggested reason that will be rejected

phrases.english: Abaye said (to him): What is the reason?
If you say it is because of the large amount of water,
phrases.notes: Two households pour more water than one

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבא's ruling in step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the משנה's rule applies even if the two apartments made an עירוב

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the amount of water does not matter
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a ברייתא: even a pit or vessel already full before שבת may receive water on שבת. So the amount of water cannot be the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: the same rule applies to a pit, a cracked earthenware vessel, a small pool, or a basin. Even though they were filled with water before שבת, one may pour water into them on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the suggested reason with a ברייתא. The ברייתא allows pouring into a pit or vessel even when it is already full, so worrying about too much water makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a completely full pit may still receive water, then extra water overflowing is clearly not a concern, as long as the pit is the proper size. More water from two households is therefore no reason to forbid it. The proposed explanation of רבא falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)? Introduces a source that contradicts what was said
A pit dug in the courtyard to collect water
A broken or cracked earthenware vessel, used here as a water receptacle

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets an important principle: once there is a properly sized receptacle, nobody worries about how much water actually runs off. That principle forces the גמרא to restate רבא's ruling.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a baraita:
phrases.notes: Here comes a source that seems to say the opposite.

phrases.english: The same rule applies to a pit,
and the same to a cracked earthenware vessel,
a small pool, or a basin:
even though they were filled with water
on Shabbat eve,
phrases.notes: Before שבת began

phrases.english: one may pour water into them on Shabbat!
phrases.notes: So the amount of water is not the concern

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a ברייתא to reject the reason proposed in step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested reason for רבא's ruling, namely the larger amount of water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows pouring even into an already full pit or vessel, which shows that the amount of water does not matter once a proper receptacle exists.

steps.title: רבא's statement must be restated
steps.stepSummary: Since the first version of רבא's statement cannot stand, the גמרא says it must have been said differently and begins the corrected version.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רבא said...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the version of רבא's statement it quoted earlier and announces a corrected version. This line is a setup, and the actual new wording of רבא follows right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "אלא אי איתמר הכי איתמר" tells us the earlier version was a mistake. The ruling that the rule applies even with an עירוב is withdrawn, since no good reason for it survived. The new wording of רבא comes in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, signals a switch away from what was said before
If it was stated, it was stated like this. A formula correcting the earlier version of a statement

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion that argues with רבא. It is the same רבא, and the גמרא is correcting how his words were reported.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated,
phrases.notes: The earlier version is being dropped

phrases.english: it was stated as follows:
Rava said:
phrases.notes: His corrected statement continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קשיא in step 30, gives up the first version of רבא's statement and starts the corrected one
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The first version of רבא's statement, that the rule applies even if they made an עירוב
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No valid reason supports it, because the amount-of-water concern was refuted by the ברייתא
